review_notes: Reviewed all 30 lines, the compact-cover and indexed-supremum lemmas used by the proofs, directed-order definitions, and current uses. The proposed generalisation is source-supported but has not been compiled.

findings.problem: Both general compactness helpers restrict the index to ℕ, although their proofs require only a nonempty upward-directed preorder. The only natural-number-specific step constructs a common upper bound using max.
findings.proposed_change:
Generalise the statements to:

theorem uniform_index_of_increasing_open_cover {ι : Type*}
    [Preorder ι] [IsDirectedOrder ι] [Nonempty ι]
    (U : ι → Set T) (hopen : ∀ k, IsOpen (U k))
    (hmono : Monotone U) (hcover : ∀ τ, ∃ k, τ ∈ U k) :
    ∃ k, ∀ τ, τ ∈ U k

theorem uniform_strict_index {ι R : Type*}
    [Preorder ι] [IsDirectedOrder ι] [Nonempty ι] [CompleteLinearOrder R]
    (F : T → R) (g : ι → T → R)
    (hopen : ∀ k, IsOpen {τ | F τ < g k τ})
    (hmono : ∀ τ, Monotone (fun k => g k τ))
    (hgap : ∀ τ, F τ < ⨆ k, g k τ) :
    ∃ k, ∀ τ, F τ < g k τ

In the first proof, replace the max construction with `obtain ⟨k, hik, hjk⟩ := exists_ge_ge i j; exact ⟨k, hmono hik, hmono hjk⟩`. The second proof otherwise remains the same: lt_iSup_iff already accepts arbitrary index types. Retain Nonempty ι: when T is empty, the hypotheses are vacuous but the conclusion still requires an index.
findings.benefit: Makes the helpers usable for directed nets, including families indexed by finite subsets, without choosing a sequential reindexing. Existing ℕ-indexed applications remain special cases, with no additional mathematical argument.

theorem exists_ge_ge [LE α] [IsDirectedOrder α] (a b : α) : ∃ c, a ≤ c ∧ b ≤ c :=
  directed_of (· ≤ ·) a b

theorem lt_iSup_iff : a < iSup f ↔ ∃ i, a < f i :=
